content:wysiwyg_basic:2:25.name: WYSIWYG
content:wysiwyg_basic:2:25.html:
Meeting the Greatest Need:

How We Help Provide Housing and Assistance

We are a nonprofit organization that works to alleviate human suffering and distress without discrimination. Our Emergency Shelter Services help all residents break the cycle of homelessness and relieve ongoing crisis by providing shelter, case management support and referrals to other agencies that specialize in the many barriers individuals experiencing homelessness encounter.

content:wysiwyg_basic:7:21.name: WYSIWYG
content:wysiwyg_basic:7:21.html:
Utility Assistance

Millions of people across the country are forced into making a choice between things like being able to keep the lights on or put food on their family's table.

We believe no one should have to make a decision like that, so we provide utility assistance and relief to those who need it. We have always fought to ensure that no one goes without heat in the coldest winters, air conditioning in the brutal summers or fresh water to drink and bathe in.

content:wysiwyg_basic:11:53.name: WYSIWYG
content:wysiwyg_basic:11:53.html:
Case Management

Our case managers concentrate on helping residents identify problems that may have contributed to their homelessness, including substance abuse, employment, education deficiencies, financial mismanagement and mental health.

Staff assist each resident in developing realistic goals to overcome their situations. Substance abuse, motivational, and ‘Life Skills Enrichment’ meetings are conducted weekly at the shelter.

content:wysiwyg_basic:16:54.html:
Building wealth & health network

This a free, 16-session curriculum over eight weeks, promoting financial literacy and self empowerment.

Participation is limited to Richmond City residents who care for one or more children, 18-years or younger.

To learn more about the Network and register for one of two informations sessions, visit our events page and click on "Building Wealth and Health Network - Cohort 3."

content:wysiwyg_basic:1785169830558:0.60.name: WYSIWYG
content:wysiwyg_basic:1785169830558:0.60.html:
Homeless Connection Line

If you are within 3 days of losing housing, contact the Homeless Crisis Line for support. The Homeless Connection Line (HCL) is managed by Homeward and is a crucial community resource for those experiencing homelessness or within a few days of losing their current housing. The HCL offers trained Diversion Specialists who can assist households within 3 days of losing their housing to problem-solve, access community resources, and connect to homeless assistance if needed.

The Central Intake System is managed by Homeward. They are the first point of entry into shelter services.

Homeless Connection Line Intake: 804.972.0813

  • Weekdays: 8:00 a.m. - 9:00 p.m.
  • Weekends: 1:00 - 9:00 p.m.
